title: CLI device authorization session create request
description: Provider identity scope configuration MUST define non-empty allowed and default scope lists containing non-empty strings without Unicode White_Space property characters, Unicode C0/C1 control characters, Unicode General Category Cf format controls, Unicode noncharacter code points, Unicode private-use code points, Unicode variation selectors, or Unicode default-ignorable code points, unique within each list, with every default scope present in the allowed list. Malformed, duplicate, empty, whitespace-bearing, control-bearing, format-control-bearing, noncharacter-bearing, private-use-bearing, variation-selector-bearing, default-ignorable-bearing, non-NFKC, or unsupported configured scopes MUST fail closed at startup and request time instead of being normalized, trimmed, sanitized, or deduplicated. Every configured scope MUST contain only Unicode scalar values and already use exact NFKC normalization; unpaired UTF-16 surrogate escapes, canonically or compatibility-equivalent alternate spellings, whitespace-bearing values, control-bearing values, format-control-bearing values, noncharacter-bearing values, private-use-bearing values, variation-selector-bearing values, and default-ignorable-bearing values MUST fail closed at startup and request time before session creation or persistence access. CLI session metadata fields cli_name, cli_version, hostname, and key_name MUST contain only Unicode scalar values. Unpaired UTF-16 surrogate escapes MUST fail closed before identity verification, provisional session insertion, API-key insertion, session mutation, or persistence access; providers MUST NOT rely on lossy UTF-8 replacement during persistence or replay comparison.

cli_name.description: CLI metadata values MUST be non-empty NFC-normalized strings without surrounding whitespace, Unicode C0/C1 control characters, Unicode line or paragraph separators, Unicode format controls, Unicode noncharacter code points, or Unicode private-use code points. Empty, non-NFC, whitespace-only, whitespace-padded, control-bearing, separator-bearing, format-control-bearing, noncharacter-bearing, or private-use-bearing values MUST fail closed before identity verification, provisional session insertion, API-key insertion, session mutation, or persistence access; providers MUST NOT normalize, trim, or sanitize caller input.

cli_version.description: CLI metadata values MUST be non-empty NFC-normalized strings without surrounding whitespace, Unicode C0/C1 control characters, Unicode line or paragraph separators, Unicode format controls, Unicode noncharacter code points, or Unicode private-use code points. Empty, non-NFC, whitespace-only, whitespace-padded, control-bearing, separator-bearing, format-control-bearing, noncharacter-bearing, or private-use-bearing values MUST fail closed before identity verification, provisional session insertion, API-key insertion, session mutation, or persistence access; providers MUST NOT normalize, trim, or sanitize caller input.

hostname.description: CLI metadata values MUST be non-empty NFC-normalized strings without surrounding whitespace, Unicode C0/C1 control characters, Unicode line or paragraph separators, Unicode format controls, Unicode noncharacter code points, or Unicode private-use code points. items.description: Every configured, requested, and persisted identity scope MUST be a non-empty Unicode-scalar string already in exact NFKC normalization and MUST NOT contain Unicode White_Space property characters, Unicode C0/C1 control characters, Unicode General Category Cf format controls, Unicode noncharacter code points, Unicode private-use code points, Unicode variation selectors, or Unicode default-ignorable code points. Canonically or compatibility-equivalent alternate spellings, whitespace-bearing values, control-bearing values, format-control-bearing values, noncharacter-bearing values, private-use-bearing values, variation-selector-bearing values, and default-ignorable-bearing values MUST fail closed before identity verification, entitlement evaluation, API-key creation, response emission, or persistence access; providers MUST NOT normalize, trim, or sanitize caller, configuration, or persisted scope values.
